nodes.summary: On `(0, 1)` the Beta`(θ₁, θ₂)` density is Wright's unnormalized density in the scaled rates `α = θ₁ / 2`, `β = θ₂ / 2`, divided by the Beta function `B(θ₁, θ₂)`.
nodes.title: Beta density as Wright's stationary density

nodes.summary: The Beta`(θ₁, θ₂)` density is analytic (`C^ω`), in particular smooth, on `(0, 1)`, so the derivatives in `flux_betaPDFReal` and `forwardEquation_betaPDFReal` exist.
nodes.title: Smoothness of the Beta density on the open unit interval

nodes.summary: On `(0, 1)` the Beta`(θ₁, θ₂)` density `π` satisfies `½ (x (1 - x) π)' - (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) / 2 · π = 0`. The identity holds for all real `θ₁, θ₂` (it is linear in `π`; Mathlib's density is identically `0` when `B(θ₁, θ₂) = 0`); `π` is a probability density when `θ₁, θ₂ > 0` (`isProbabilityMeasureBeta`).
nodes.title: Zero probability flux (Wright 1931)

nodes.summary: On `(0, 1)` the Beta`(θ₁, θ₂)` density `π` solves the stationary Fokker–Planck equation `½ (a π)'' - (b π)' = 0` with `a(x) = x (1 - x)` and `b(x) = (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) / 2`. Holds for all real `θ₁, θ₂` (see `flux_betaPDFReal`).
nodes.title: Stationary forward equation (Wright 1931)

nodes.summary: For `θ₁, θ₂ > 0` and `f` twice continuously differentiable on `[0, 1]`, `L f` is integrable against Wright's stationary law `Beta(θ₁, θ₂)`.
nodes.title: Integrability of the mutation generator under Wright's stationary law

nodes.summary: One generation of the Wright–Fisher chain on `M` gene copies (`M = 2N`): mutation moves the frequency `x` to `p' = mutatedFreq u₁ u₂ x`, then the new count is `Binomial(M, p')`. With `u₁ = θ₁ / (2M)`, `u₂ = θ₂ / (2M)` (`θᵢ = 4N uᵢ`), the expected change of frequency per `2N = M` generations is exactly the drift coefficient of `mutationGenerator`: `M · (E[k / M] - x) = (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) / 2`, for every `M`.
nodes.title: Drift of the Wright–Fisher chain with mutation (Ewens 2004, ch. 4)

nodes.summary: In the setting of `integral_binomial_mutatedFreq_drift`, the scaled second moment of the frequency change is `M · E[(k / M - x) ^ 2] = p' (1 - p') + (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) ^ 2 / (4M)` with `p' = mutatedFreq u₁ u₂ x = x + (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) / (2M)`. As `M → ∞` with `θ₁, θ₂, x` fixed this tends to `x (1 - x)`, the diffusion coefficient of `mutationGenerator` (the limit itself is not stated here).
nodes.title: Infinitesimal variance of the Wright–Fisher chain with mutation

nodes.summary: For `θ₁, θ₂ > 0` and every `f` twice continuously differentiable on `[0, 1]`, `∫ L f d(Beta(θ₁, θ₂)) = 0`.
nodes.title: Weak stationarity of Wright's law (Wright 1931; Ewens 2004, ch. 4)

nodes.summary: For `θ₁, θ₂ > 0` and every `f` twice continuously differentiable on `[0, 1]`, `∫₀¹ (L f)(x) π(x) dx = 0` for the Beta`(θ₁, θ₂)` density `π`. (`L f` uses `deriv`, which agrees with the one-sided derivatives inside `(0, 1)`; its values at the endpoints do not affect the integral.) The proof is integration by parts: `L f · π = (x ^ θ₁ (1 - x) ^ θ₂ f' / (2 B(θ₁, θ₂)))'` on `(0, 1)` because the flux vanishes, and this…
nodes.title: Weak stationarity of Wright's law (density form)

nodes.summary: For `θ₁, θ₂ > 0` and `f` twice continuously differentiable on `[0, 1]`, `L f · π` is integrable on `[0, 1]`, so the integral in `integral_mutationGenerator_mul_betaPDFReal` is a genuine (not junk) value.
nodes.title: Integrability of the mutation generator against the Beta density

nodes.summary: Allele frequency after one generation of two-way mutation, before random sampling: an `a` copy mutates to `A` with probability `u₁` and an `A` copy to `a` with probability `u₂`, so the frequency `x` of `A` becomes `(1 - u₂) x + u₁ (1 - x) ∈ [0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Allele frequency after one generation of two-way mutation

nodes.summary: The generator applied to the heterozygosity `H(x) = 2x (1 - x)`: `L H = -2x (1 - x) + (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) (1 - 2x)` (drift decreases `H` at rate `1`, mutation restores it).
nodes.title: Mutation generator applied to heterozygosity

nodes.summary: The generator applied to the frequency itself is the mutation drift: `L x = (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) / 2`.
nodes.title: Mutation generator applied to the allele frequency

nodes.summary: Without mutation the generator is the neutral Wright–Fisher generator `generator 0`.
nodes.title: Mutation generator without mutation is the neutral generator

nodes.summary: The backward generator of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with two-way mutation, time in units of `2N` generations and scaled mutation rates `θ₁ = 4N u₁` (towards the allele) and `θ₂ = 4N u₂` (away from it): `(L f)(x) = x (1 - x) / 2 · f''(x) + (θ₁ (1 - x) - θ₂ x) / 2 · f'(x)`.
nodes.title: Wright–Fisher generator with two-way mutation
